title: Assured AI: requirements for the programme GitHub projects

sections.title: Assured AI: requirements for the programme GitHub projects
sections.extract: Build specification for an AI agent Document control; Detail Purpose; Requirements for an AI agent to set up two organisation-level GitHub Projects for the WHO Assured AI project (Gates Foundation grant INV-108130): a partner-facing programme project and a private programme management (PM) project, both linked to the workstream projects Version; 0.3.6, 15 October 2026 Status; Approved for a pilot build. The build

sections.title: 1. What the build must achieve
sections.extract: Workstream leads run their own delivery in their own projects. Partners and WHO see one shared programme picture. The PM keeps dependencies, reviews, risks and decisions in a private control layer. The same issue is never copied to make any of this work. The principle the agent must follow: issue fields hold the shared values; projects are different views of them. Layer; GitHub object; Purpose; Main users Programme

sections.title: 1.1 Terms used in this document
sections.extract: Term; Meaning PM & Architecture Integration; The programme manager role for the project. Referred to as "the PM" Technical Integration Lead; The person who confirms that technical components are ready to integrate and validates them (DP-05a) Workstream (WS1 to WS5); The five delivery streams of the project, each with its own lead. "Platform" covers shared hosting and engineering Epic code; The reference for each

sections.title: 2. Design principles
sections.extract: ID; Principle DP-01; Create once, show many times. One issue can appear in several projects. Never clone an issue to report its status somewhere else. DP-02; Workstream leads own their delivery. The agent creates programme epics and the workstream template. It does not create features or stories in workstream repositories. DP-03; Programme work is not sprint work. Sprints are managed inside the workstream projects.

sections.title: 3. Decisions needed before the build
sections.extract: The agent may carry out step 1 of section 13 (pre-flight) at any time. It must not configure or create anything from step 2 onward until every decision relevant to that step is confirmed. Each decision has a recommended default. ID; Decision; Recommended default; Why it matters BD-01; GitHub organisation; Decided: the existing World Health Organization organisation, shared with other WHO teams. Login:

sections.title: 4. Structure
sections.extract: GitHub organisation: [BD-01] │ ├── repo aai-programme Partner-visible │ Epics, milestone issues, research question issues, │ workstream directory, roadmap docs │ ├── repo aai-pm Restricted (PM only) │ Programme dependencies (D-numbers), decisions (DEC-numbers), │ material assumptions, scripts and their settings │ ├── repo aai-ws1 … aai-ws5 Created by the build once each lead is confirmed; the lead holds Maintain │

sections.title: 5.1 Issue types
sections.extract: Shared organisation rule. The World Health Organization organisation is shared with other WHO teams. Every organisation issue field and every new issue type created for this project is prefixed AAI, for example AAI Workstream or AAI Decision, so it cannot be confused with or collide with another team's. Existing generic issue types (such as Epic, Feature or Task) may be reused if the owners agree. Fields are pinned

sections.title: 5.2 Hierarchy
sections.extract: Sub-issues represent work breakdown only: Epic, then Feature, then Story or Spike. Research questions are not parents of epics. An item links to research questions through the rq: labels, which list every question it contributes to, including its primary one. The Primary research question field records the main question only, for grouping. The research question issue holds the question, its sub-questions, the

sections.title: 5.3 Fields shown on each issue type
sections.extract: Organisation issue fields must be pinned to issue types to appear on the issue form. GitHub allows up to 10 pinned fields per issue type. Pin only these: Issue type; Pinned fields Epic; Workstream, Programme status, Pipeline stage, Integration readiness, Gates output, Primary research question, Start date, Target date, Backlog ref Milestone; Programme status, Gates output, Start date, Target date Research question;

sections.extract: Create these in every repository listed in section 4. Workstream leads should keep them unchanged. sections.title: 7.4 Fallback if issue fields are unavailable
sections.extract: If BD-05 or BD-06 cannot be met: 1. Create the section 7.1 fields as project fields, with identical names and options, in both programme projects and in the template. 2. Build a sync job: a GitHub Action that runs daily and on demand, copies the section 7.1 values from Assured AI Programme into PM Control, and reports any mismatches. 3. Record this in the build report. Do not mix the two approaches.

sections.title: 8. Views
sections.extract: Each view lists its layout, which items it shows, how they are grouped and sorted, and the columns to display.

sections.extract: ID; View; Layout; Items; Group and sort; Columns P1; Master programme (PM); Table; Same as V1; Same as V1; V1 columns, plus Risk status, Dependency refs, Review status, Decision ref P2; Programme dependencies; Table; Dependency issues from aai-pm; Group by Workstream of the waiting epic; sort by Target date (used as needed-by date); Title (starts with D-number), Workstream, Target date, Programme status, Risk

sections.title: 8.3 Assured AI Workstream Template
sections.extract: Create this as an organisation project template. It contains: the issue fields from section 7.1, shown as columns a Sprint iteration field (two weeks) three views: Sprint board (current sprint, grouped by built-in Status), Backlog (table of all open items), and Roadmap Project templates do not copy auto-add workflows. The template README must tell leads how to set up auto-add for their own repository.

sections.title: 9. Dependencies
sections.extract: DEP-01. Ordinary technical dependencies use GitHub's native "blocked by" and "blocking" relationships between the issues concerned. Workstream teams create these themselves. They are visible to partners. DEP-02. A dependency becomes a D-number issue in aai-pm only if it is programme-significant: it crosses workstreams or partners and needs a deadline, negotiation, escalation or an assessment of consequences. DEP-03.

sections.title: 10. Linking to workstream projects
sections.extract: ID; Requirement LINK-01; Create a pinned issue in aai-programme titled "Workstream directory". For each workstream it lists the lead, the repository and the project URL. Leave entries blank until leads supply them. LINK-02; Both programme project READMEs link to the directory issue. The PM Control README also lists each lead. LINK-03; The template README tells leads to link back to Assured AI Programme. LINK-04;

sections.title: 11. Automation
sections.extract: ID; Requirement AUTO-01; Auto-add to Assured AI Programme: all issues in aai-programme, and workstream issues labelled thin-slice or sprint-demo. GitHub limits the number of auto-add workflows per project depending on the plan. If the limit is reached, use a GitHub Action instead and record this. AUTO-02; Auto-add to PM Control: all issues in aai-programme and aai-pm. AUTO-03; A GitHub Action, using the BD-08

sections.title: 12. Pilot build
sections.extract: Before any bulk import, the agent builds and tests this small set, each item clearly marked as a pilot: 1 epic in aai-programme 2 features in two different workstream repositories, as sub-issues of the epic 1 native "blocked by" relationship between the two features 1 D-number issue in aai-pm 1 research question issue 1 milestone issue 1 item with Review type set 1 item labelled thin-slice 1 item labelled

sections.title: 13. Build sequence
sections.extract: 1. Pre-flight. Confirm the section 3 decisions are recorded. Inspect existing issue types, issue fields, organisation issue-field headroom, project field counts, projects, teams, repository policies, SSO/EMU constraints and permissions in the organisation. Reuse compatible organisation configuration and do not create anything that duplicates something already there. 2. Organisation setup. An organisation owner

sections.extract: Input; Used for Epics import CSV and its gh CLI script; Epics Roadmap Markdown with the Mermaid Gantt chart; aai-programme README; start and target dates Gates outputs list with output months; Milestone issues and Gates output options Research questions R1 to R7, with sub-questions; Research question issues Dependency register D01 to D29; D-number issues in aai-pm Workstream directory details; Directory issue,

sections.title: 15. Acceptance criteria
sections.extract: ID; Criterion AC-01; Both programme projects and the template exist in the agreed organisation, with the agreed access AC-02; Every view in section 8 exists and shows the intended items AC-03; The section 7.1 fields are organisation issue fields, and no project field duplicates them (unless the section 7.4 fallback was used) AC-04; Every epic from the CSV appears once in V1 and once in P1 AC-05; Every Gates output

sections.title: 16. Build report
sections.extract: The agent hands back a short report covering: what was created, what existing organisation configuration was reused, the organisation issue-field headroom and each project's total field count after the build the pass or fail result for each pilot test and acceptance criterion any fallback used, and why permissions that still need an organisation owner every value left empty because it was missing from the inputs

sections.title: 17. Open points to be confirmed by the PM
sections.extract: The start date of the first sprint (S0), used for the Sprint iteration field in the workstream template. The final Gates output list and output months. Whether Gates Foundation contacts get access to Assured AI Programme. For each workstream, which partner source-code repositories stay external, and how WHO issues link to them (BD-02b). The final workstream names used as Workstream field options (WS1 to WS5), before

sections.title: 18. Out of scope
sections.extract: Workstream backlogs, and any views specific to one workstream. A partner contribution or partner commitments view. Importing the PM's existing decision log or the project asset inventory. Making any project or repository public. Changing organisation-wide GitHub security or access policies.
